title: Runtime compatibility contract and upgrade trajectories
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Teams need a single, machine-readable compatibility contract and a clear upgrade trajectory for the serving runtime so customers and internal services can plan non-disruptive upgrades. Current expectations are scattered across PRDs, release notes, and ad-hoc email threads. This ticket defines the semantic versioning policy for the runtime (what constitutes a breaking change), the LTS/Stable/Canary channels with supported durations and backport rules, and the tooling required to publish and enforce compatibility metadata. Deliverables: (1) a compatibility contract format (JSON headers + release metadata), (2) specification for allowed ABI/behavior changes per semver increment, (3) rollout gating checklist and automated CI validations, (4) a migration assistant CLI that surfaces explicit migration steps and risk classification, (5) documentation and example annotated releases used for a runtime-2.0 canary in April.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility contract documented in Confluence with schema example and a machine-readable JSON header format
CI validations added: automated ABI check, protobuf compatibility test, and end-to-end SDK smoke tests run for each semantic increment
LTS/stable/canary channel definitions committed; policy includes support windows, backport policy, and upgrade freeze rules
Migration assistant CLI (runtime-upgrade-helper) prototype that ingests old->new version and emits a migration plan with affected APIs, config flags, and recommended rollout gates
Release pipeline annotates each published artifact with contract metadata and publishes a human-friendly migration note in the release changelog

notes: Trade-offs: Stronger compatibility guarantees slow feature velocity; we propose a 2-week experimental freeze window for major versions and a fast path for security fixes
Decision: Semantic rules emphasize observable behavior (API payload shapes, KV cache persistence format, kernel behavioral contracts) over private internal refactors
Edge case: Model format changes that alter tokenization behavior are treated as breaking unless a compatibility layer exists
Backport policy: Only P0 security and P0 runtime-availability fixes are backported to LTS branches; non-critical bug fixes go to Stable and next minor
